SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Case against Ling Zoong Kwei (林仲達) arrested on
Broadway on May 7, 1933.

Made by D.S. Pitts.. Forwarded by D.S.Pitts. D.I.

Enquiries made through Supt. Tan Shao Liang from the
local Bureau of Public Safety show that Ling Zoong Kwei,
who was arrested by the Municipal Police at the request of
the Chinese authorities on Broadway on May 7, 1933, was
sent to Nanking on May 11. He is the alleged secretary of
the Communist Party's Seamen's Union of Foreign Steamers.
Enquiries made by Mr. Gibson of the local offices of
the Robert Dollar Line to verify the prisoner's statement
have so far proved unsuccessful, but he is retaining a
photograph of Ling, and in the event of any further in-
formation coming to his notice regarding the activities or
antecedents of the man in question, he will not fail to let
us know.

D.S. Pitts

D. S.

主题（全称） 关于林仲達（Ling Zoong Kwei）一案，该人于1933年5月7日在百老汇路被捕。

制作人：D.S. Pitts。转发人：D.S. Pitts，巡官。

经通过谭绍良（Tan Shao Liang）警长向当地公安局查询得知，林仲達应中国当局要求，于1933年5月7日在百老汇路被工部局警务处逮捕，并于5月11日被送往南京。据称他是共产党外籍轮船海员工会的秘书。
罗伯特·美元轮船公司（Robert Dollar Line）上海办事处的吉布森先生（Mr. Gibson）为核实囚犯的陈述所进行的调查迄今未有结果，但他保留了林的照片，一旦获悉有关该人活动或背景的任何进一步消息，他将立即通知我们。

D.S. Pitts

May 17, 1933.

LIM CHUNG KWEI

MR. H. E. GIBSON
SHANGHAI OFFICE.

Your SC-12/HEG.

I sent you via the President Hoover a radio
advising that we have no record of this man under this name,
and that he positively was not on the President Madison at
the time of the accident. This man's face appears very
familiar, and I am certain I have seen him at Hongkong, but
I cannot identify him. I showed his photograph to the #1
of the President Madison, and the #1 states positively that
he has never seen the man, and that most certainly he was not
on the President Madison's Crew. If you could give me any
of his aliases I might be able to identify him under some
other name.

I am returning herewith the photograph, but
if you wish us to make further enquiries concerning him,
please send a photograph.

Yours very truly,

Further to a report dated May 15, 1933 on the subject
of the arrest of Ling Zoong Kwei, I have to state that Mr.
Gibson has forwarded a photograph of the accused to the
Robert Dollar Line, Hong Kong, from whom a radio message as
follows has been received by Mr. Gibson :
"YOUR LETTER SC-12 NO RECORD UNDER THIS NAME
POSITIVELY WAS NOT ON THE MADISON DURING
ACCIDENT FACE FAMILIAR BUT CANNOT IDENTIFY"
Copies of the letters received from Mr. Gibson relat-
ing to this matter are submitted herewith.
From a perusal of these letters it will be seen that
when he made his statement to the Municipal Police, the
prisoner was deliberately lying.
A further report will be submitted in due course upon
the result of the enquiries made by the Hong Kong Branch
of the Robert Dollar Line in regard to the antecedents and
activities of Ling Zoong Kwei.

LIM CHUNG KWEI

MR. T. R. WILSON,
HONGKONG.

        I am enclosing copy of a photograph of Lim Chung Kwei.
This man has several aliases and is supposed to be an active
member of the Red Seamen's Union.    He was arrested by the
police two days ago with a considerable quantity of communist
literature in his possession.

        According to his statement he was two years on the
SS PRES. LINCOLN and on the SS "PRES. MADISON at the time of
the accident in Seattle.    He returned to Hongkong by the SS
PRES. CLEVELAND and later on was shipped up here by a vessel
of the Java-China-Japan Line.

        The Shanghai Police have asked me to assist them in
verifying this man's statement, and if he was actually employed
on our vessels.    According to the police this man is reported
by the Nanking Government as being a very dangerous man,
therefore, any information that you can give me would be
greatly appreciated.

        Request that you kindly return the photograph.

                    Yours very truly,

        现附上林仲魁的照片副本。此人拥有多个别名，据信是红色海员工会的活跃成员。两天前他被警方逮捕，当时身上携带大量共产主义宣传品。

        根据其陈述，他在“林肯总统号”（SS PRES. LINCOLN）轮上工作了两年，在西雅图发生事故时正在“麦迪逊总统号”（SS "PRES. MADISON"）轮上。他乘坐“克利夫兰总统号”（SS PRES. CLEVELAND）轮返回香港，后来由荷印日轮船公司（Java-China-Japan Line）的一艘船只运送到这里。

        上海警方请求我协助核实此人的陈述，以及他是否确实在我们的船只上受雇。据警方称，南京政府报告此人为极度危险人物，因此，如果您能提供任何信息，我将不胜感激。

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to that part of the statement made by
Ling Zoong Kwei, who was arrested on May 7, 1933 by the Mun-
icipal Police at the instance of the Bureau of Public Safety,
in which he affirmed that he resided for one night in a hotel
in the vicinity of the Customs Jetty, I have to report that
efforts made by C.D.C. 280 attached to this Section to lo-
cate this hotel have failed to materialise.
Armed with a photograph of the arrested man C.D.C. 280
has visited over twenty hotels in the Central and Louza
districts, but in no case could the management of the hotels
identify the picture shown them .
Attached herewith is a list of the hotelds visited.
A photograph of the accused has also been handed to Mr.
Gibson of the Robert Dollar Line, in whose employ the prisoner
stated he had been for some years. Mr. Gibson has prom-
ised to transmit this photograph to the Hong-Kong Branch of
his company for purposes of identification and enquiry as
to the accused's antecedents and activities whilst in the
Colony.

关于林仲達于1933年5月7日应公安局要求被工部局警务处逮捕时所作的陈述中提及他在海关码头附近的一家旅馆住了一晚的部分，我必须报告，隶属于本科的华捕侦探 280 号（C.D.C. 280）为寻找该旅馆所做的努力未能取得结果。
华捕侦探 280 号手持被捕者的照片，走访了中央区和老闸区（Louza）的二十多家旅馆，但在任何情况下，旅馆管理层都无法识别出示给他们的照片。
随函附上已走访旅馆的清单。
被告的照片也已交给罗伯特·美元轮船公司的吉布森先生，囚犯声称他曾为该公司工作多年。吉布森先生承诺将此照片转交其公司香港分公司，以便确认身份并调查被告在该殖民地期间的背景和活動。

Charge Application.
Application is hereby made to the S. S. D. Court that the above named person who was arrested at about 1.40 p.m. on 7/5/33, on Broadway as a suspected communist, be handed over to the Chinese Authorities.
Compt:- Liu Chi Sun

HIGH COURT.

Proceedings. Mr K.S.Kum appeared for the Police.
Mr Kum:- In this case the P.S.Bureau apply for the handing over of the accused who was arrested at about 1.40 p.m. on the 7/5/33 on the Broadway, by S.P.C.248 at the request of Liu Chi Sum, ex-communist and now an accredited agent of the Nanking Authorities. In possession of the accused at the time of his arrest were found these ten books, all of which are of a communistic nature. When questioned by the Police at the Station the accused stated that he was residing at an Hotel situated near the Customs Jetty, accompanied by the Detectives he was taken there but was unable to point out any hotel.
C.D.C.116:- The accused was brought to the station by S.P.C.248 and the informer. The informer stated that the accused is a communist. The accused gave an address on the Bund as his residence, we took the accused to the Bund but he was unable to point out the hotel. The accused stated that he had purchased the books found in his possession from a shop on Broadway.
Dan Yoong Sing Representative of the P.S.Bureau:- The informer who requested that the accused be arrested is an excommunist, and now in the employ of the Nanking Authorities. The informer knows that the accused is a communist.
Liu Chi Sun Rep. Of the Nanking Authorities:- I was a member of the Communist Part, but surrendered myself to the Nanking Authorities and am now an agent. I was appointed to the Shanghai District a month ago. The accused is employed as secretary

My name is Ling Zoong Kwei alias Ling Choong Wen(          ).36.
married, native or Shih Tsu Village, Hsin Wei Hsien, Kwangtung.
When I was 9 years old I studied for 4 years in a Primary
School in my native place. From that time I acted as a farmer in
my native country until I was 21 years of age.
Then for 4½ years I was employed as a boy in various clubs in
Hongkong, where I got my first knowledge of English, which I now
speak fairly well.
After that I obtained employment as a boy on steamers plying
between Hongkong and Canton. Then I joined Jardine Matheson's and
stayed on their boats between Canton and Shanghai for about a year.
Then I obtained a job as a boy on the C.P.R.'s "Empress of
Asia" and remained on her for 18 months. Leaving this position I
worked on the Blue Funnel's S.S."Tyndaras" on the Hongkong Van-
couver run for about a year.
My wages on these boats vaired from $10. to $20.00 per month.
Then whilst in Hongkong I joined the Dollar S.S.Co's S.S.
"President Lincoln" as a boy and remained on her for some 2 years,
constantly going backwards and forwards over the Pacific. I then
was transfered to the "President Madison" on which I remained until
it sunk in Seattle in the early part of April of this year.
After this incident I went to Hongkong on the "President Cleve-
land still working as a boy. I arrived there on or about April 25,
1933 when I was discharged.
Whilst in Hongkong I was staying at 128 Des Voeur Road,Central
premises housing Dan Myi Kok(      ) a Seamen's Club. Some of my
papers and belonging are there now,including my Seaman's Discharge

我叫林佐贵 ( Ling Zoong Kwei )，又名林崇文 ( Ling Choong Wen )(          )。36岁。
已婚，籍贯广东省新会县石咀村。
我9岁时在家乡的一所小学读了4年书。从那时起直到21岁，我一直在家乡务农。
随后4年半，我在香港各家俱乐部当侍役，在那里初次接触英语，我现在英语说得相当好。
之后，我在往返于香港和广州之间的轮船上担任侍役。后来我加入怡和洋行，在其往返于广州和上海之间的船只上工作了约一年。
接着，我在加拿大太平洋铁路公司 ( C.P.R. ) 的“亚细亚皇后号”轮船上找到一份侍役的工作，并在那裡待了18个月。离开该职位后，我在蓝烟囱轮船公司的“廷达拉斯号”轮船上工作，该船航行于香港至温哥华航线，历时约一年。
我在这些船上的月薪从10美元到20美元不等。
后来在香港，我加入美元轮船公司的“林肯总统号”轮船担任侍役，并在那裡待了约2年，频繁往返于太平洋两岸。随后我被调往“麦迪逊总统号”，一直工作到今年4月初该船在西雅图沉没。
事故发生后，我乘坐“克利夫兰总统号”前往香港，继续担任侍役。我于1933年4月25日左右抵达那里，随即被解雇。
在香港期间，我住在中环德辅道128号，那里是丹义阁 ( Dan Myi Kok )(      ) 海员俱乐部的所在地。我的一些文件和物品仍留在那里，包括我的海员解职

    It was my intention to apply for a job in Shanghai as a boy in

    Immediately after my arrival here at 11 a.m. May 6 I was taken

remember by a wharf usher who met me at the Customs Jetty where I
disembarked alone. The number of my room, for which I paid $2.50
